subject: Order Form / MSA — indemnity split proposal and routing
messages:
From: Rachel Connor <rachel.connor@helix.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@helix.ai, tom.alvarez@helix.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: MSA / Order Form — indemnity ask and routing

Hannah / Ben —

Thanks for the call earlier. Procurement asked me to capture the remaining open items on indemnity so our legal team can finish review. Two specific asks from Helix:

1) We need a clearer defense control path for third-party IP claims that result from model outputs (patent assertions on generated content). Helix prefers Redwood to accept defense when the content was generated from customer prompts that include Helix proprietary data.

2) Helix cannot accept unlimited duty to indemnify for third-party claims stemming from data the customer controls. We propose a carve-out: customer-originated prompts/data are outside Redwood's indemnity, and Redwood would cover only model defects or tiered responsibility when Redwood fine-tuned models on Redwood-managed datasets.

I've attached our proposed redline (Helix_proposed_redline.pdf) and included procurement/contact Tom for contract timing. Can you confirm Redwood's preferred approach and estimated timeline for a final position?

Appreciate a short call if needed.

—Rachel
Rachel Connor
Head of Legal Ops, Helix.ai
Attachments: Helix_proposed_redline.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Connor <rachel.connor@helix.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2025 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — indemnity ask and routing

Rachel —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redline. We reviewed with Legal Ops and have two practical paths to propose so procurement can decide tradeoffs quickly:

Option A — Standard defend-and-indemnify for third‑party IP claims where Redwood: (i) controls the model weights/updates (i.e., Redwood-managed fine tuning), and (ii) the alleged infringement arises from Redwood-generated model logic (not from customer-supplied proprietary content). Defense control will be Redwood-led with obligation to consult Helix on significant litigation steps.

Option B — Limited indemnity with a stronger carve-out for customer-originated prompts/data. Redwood will accept reimbursement (costs of remediation and settled amounts) where evidence shows a model defect attributable to Redwood-managed training pipeline, up to a cap tied to the order form (suggested: 12 months of committed fees). Defense control remains with the customer for claims primarily driven by customer data.

We're attaching an internal redline (Redwood_MSA_redline_v2.docx) that implements Option B with suggested language for notice, evidence preservation, and an escrow-based threshold for defense transfer.

Can you confirm which option Helix prefers? If you want to keep the call cadence, we can do 30 minutes tomorrow; otherwise we can exchange comments in DocuSign.

Next steps we propose internally: loop in Procurement / Legal lead and, if Option B is acceptable, have Counsel (Kimberly) run a short risk memo to approve the cap/escrow approach.

Best —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline_v2.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2025 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — indemnity ask and routing

Hannah / Ben —

Quick legal note on the two options:

- Option A (Redwood-led defense when Redwood-managed model code/weights are implicated) is cleaner for Helix but increases Redwood's exposure. If we go this route, we should tighten the notice/evidence window (10 business days) and require Helix to preserve prompts/output logs and provide clear reproducibility markers. Also add a mutual cooperation clause (Redwood remains able to settle subject to reasonableness review).

- Option B (reimbursement + cap) is lower risk commercially. The suggested cap tied to 12 months of committed fees is typical for order-form level deals but we should reserve the right to take over defense if Redwood is already materially controlling remediation (to protect Redwood from operational burden).

Specific redline suggestions (high level):
1) Add a definition: "Customer-Originated Content" = prompts, embeddings, or datasets uploaded by customer. Exclude this from Redwood indemnity.
2) Evidence gate: require Helix to provide an artefact package (prompt, output, environment snapshot, timestamped logs).
3) Escrow threshold: claims requiring Redwood to assume defense must exceed $250k or be part of a class-action / injunctive relief that materially affects service.
4) Insurance offset: allow Redwood to offset with available insurance proceeds.

If Hannah/Ben want, I can draft a 1-page counsel memo that compares liability exposure under A vs B with recommended mitigation language. That will speed procurement.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@helix.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: rachel.connor@helix.ai, procurement@helix.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 09:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — indemnity ask and routing

Hannah / Team —

Appreciate the quick review. Helix prefers Option A for customer-facing simplicity, but we can accept a narrowly tailored evidence gate if Redwood will take defense. Key points from Helix Legal:

- Defense control: Helix wants Redwood to accept defense when the claim arises from outputs generated by Redwood-managed model variants (i.e., Helix is not fine-tuning in their environment). Helix will provide preserved prompt/output logs as described.
- Escalation: For claims under $100k, Helix is OK with reimbursement; for claims >= $100k Redwood should assume defense if evidence shows model causation.
- Timing: Procurement aims to complete execution by Friday EOD. We will upload our counter-redline to DocuSign and start the routing (link below).

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/doclink/ABC123-Helix
Attachment: Helix_proposed_redline.pdf

If Kimberly can send the short memo today comparing exposure under Option A vs Option B, that will help procurement present to their GC. Otherwise Helix will flag this as a commercial exception to be approved by their CFO.

Thanks —
Tom
Tom Alvarez
Procurement Lead, Helix.ai

Team —

Summary and immediate next steps based on Helix's preference for Option A:

1) Kimberly — please draft the 1-page memo comparing A vs B with recommended escrow threshold and the proposed $250k vs Helix's $100k split. Focus on: exposure delta, insurance offset, and recommended operational gating (logs + 10 business day notice). If we can keep the memo under 2 pages, Procurement will likely accept it for GC review.
2) Ben — patch the Redwood_MSA_redline_v2.docx to incorporate defense-control language but include the evidence gate and settlement-governor (Redwood must get reasonable approval for any settlement > $50k). Put that file into DocuSign as a counter to the Helix upload if Kimberly flags Option A as acceptable.
3) Irene — prepare a short playbook for the customer success/ops team: what logs we need, how to preserve them, and the internal contact list for evidence collection. Include retention windows and an ownership matrix.

Timeline requested: memo + redline updates by EOD tomorrow; enable one 30-minute alignment call Thursday AM if needed. I will manage the procurement thread and push for the Friday EOD execution target.

I'll keep Helix updated on progress and call out any material changes to the cap/threshold.

Thanks all —
Hannah
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
